chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: My father said: Muhammad ibn Abu al-Sahban said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi said: Aban al-Ahmar narrated to me from the Truth-teller, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both)

A man came to him and said to him: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, admonish me with an exhortation.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has guaranteed sustenance, then why is your concern [for accumulation]? And if sustenance is allocated, then why is your greed? And if reckoning is true, then why is your gathering [of wealth]? And if replacement from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is true, then why is your miserliness? And if the punishment from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the Hellfire, then why is your sinning? And if death is true, then why is your happiness [in worldly life]? And if presentation before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is true, then why is your cunning? And if Satan is an enemy, then why is your heedlessness? And if crossing the Bridge is true, then why is your pride? And if everything is by decree and destiny, then why is your grief? And if the world is perishable, then why is your tranquility [in it] towards it?'
ai.seo_question: What are the theological reasons for worldly anxiety and greed according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this famous *maw'iza* (exhortation) from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs a dialectical method to dismantle worldly anxieties by linking them directly to core theological tenets like divine provision (*rizq*) and predestination (*qadr*). This narration is pivotal in Shia scholarship for illustrating how intellectual acceptance of God's attributes must translate into psychological tranquility (*ittima'in*) and ethical consistency, warning against the hypocrisy of claiming faith while remaining enslaved by greed, pride, or fear.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 21. Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (RA) said: My father said: Muhammad ibn Abu al-Suhban said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi said, Aban al-Ahmar related to me that

A man came to al-Sadiq Ja`far ibn Muhammad (AS) and said: “May my father and mother be your ransom! Admonish me with an exhortation.” So he (AS) said: If Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Sustainer, then why do you worry? If sustenance is allocated with fairness, then why are you greedy? If you will be held accountable, then why do you save? If Allah, the mighty and High, is generous, then why are you miserly? If the punishment from Allah, the Mighty and High, is the Hell, then why do you sin? If death is true, then why are you happy? If all actions are fro Allah, the Mighty and High, then why do you cheat? If Satan is your open enemy, then why do you neglect (your duties)? If crossing the Bridge (al-Sirat) is true, then why are you proud? If everything has been decreed, then why do you grieve? If the word is perishable, then why are you attached to it?
